paper_type_evidence.quote: Recently, ALMA observations of the CO(3-2) emission of the circumstellar envelope have been made publicly available (ALMA 0100334[3/5]). The present work presents an analysis of these data

question.value: What are the morphology and kinematics of the CO(3-2) gas envelope of the Mira binary W Aql, from spatially resolved Doppler velocity spectra?

evidence.quote: The present work presents an analysis of these data, which provide for the first time spatially resolved Doppler velocity spectra.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$$<$2012.1.00524.S$>$.

method.value: Compare azimuthally averaged flux vs R for ALMA and ACA to find short-spacing cutoff; restrict ALMA to R<4'' and velocities -14 to 18 km/s

evidence.quote: Accordingly, in what follows, we restrict the analysis of the ALMA data to angular distances from the central star not exceeding $4''$

key_parameters.value: V_x* = 3.2 km/s mean velocity of selected sample

evidence.quote: The mean velocity of the selected sample of observations is $V_x^{\ast}$=3.2 km s$^{-1}$.

validation.value: Compared ACA profile with APEX single-dish profile

evidence.quote: While the line profile observed by ACA is in good agreement with that observed in the single dish APEX data

analysis_steps.goal: Map flux and mean velocity vs azimuth

method.value: Average flux and mean Doppler velocity in R bins and 15 deg phi bins; fit sine waves V0+V1cos(phi-phi0)

evidence.quote: Sine wave fits of the form $<V_x -V_ x^\ast>=V_0 +V_ 1 \cos(\varphi-\varphi_0)$

fitting.value: sine wave fit, method not stated

evidence.loc: Morphology and kinematics of the CSE at short distances ($R<4''$)
evidence.quote: Sine wave fits of the form $<V_x -V_ x^\ast>=V_0 +V_ 1 \cos(\varphi-\varphi_0)$ give $V_0 =0.87$ km s$^{-1}$, $V_1 =0.75$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\varphi_0 =176^\circ$ for $R<2''$
However, the quality of the fit is poor in the latter case

method.value: Exponential fit A0 exp(-R/R0) for R<3''; elongation angles maximizing flux-weighted cos^2 and velocity asymmetry in 0.5'' R bins

evidence.quote: directions of elongation are defined as the values of angle $\varphi_0$ that maximize the mean values of $\cos^2(\varphi-\varphi_0)$

evidence.loc: Morphology and kinematics of the CSE at short distances ($R<4''$)
evidence.quote: An exponential fit of the form $A_0 e^{-R/R_0}$ for $R<3''$ gives $A_0=4.18$ Jy km s$^{-1}$ arcsec$^{-2}$ and $R_0=1.08''$.

results_numeric.quantity: Sine fit R<2'': V0, V1, phi0
Line profile slope in central region

evidence.quote: the red-shifted side being enhanced with respect to the blue-shifted side by $\sim2$% per km s$^{-1}$
the $R<2''$ region is red-shifted with respect to the $2''<R<4''$ region by $\sim2.1$ km s$^{-1}$
extending up to at least $22''$ at a typical level of $\sim32$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ arcsec$^{-2}$

findings_qualitative.value: Emission is elongated NE/SW with a velocity gradient perpendicular to the star-companion line; elongation and velocity gradient rotate with radius.

evidence.quote: one evolves from a morphology elongated along the east/west direction with a velocity gradient directed along this same direction to a morphology elongated along the north-east/south-west direction

claims.hypothesis: Is the CSE of W Aql asymmetric in morphology and kinematics at short distances?
claims.experiment: Azimuthal analysis of ALMA CO(3-2) maps for R<4''
claims.result: Flux enhancements and velocity asymmetry with sine-wave amplitudes ~0.75-1.7 km/s, direction evolving with R
claims.finding: Complex, non-spherical wind structure; expansion vs rotation interpretation cannot be distinguished

evidence.quote: At short distances ($R<4''$) the present data do not allow for choosing between these two interpretations

claims.hypothesis: Does CO emission extend to large distances consistent with dust?
claims.experiment: ACA flux vs phi in R bins 5-20''
claims.result: Enhancements west for 5-10'' and at ±60° from east for 15-20''
claims.finding: Consistent with far-IR dust emission, but details such as a spiral are not revealed

evidence.quote: is consistent with the results obtained earlier from dust emission in the far infrared

limitations_admitted.value: Short observing time, single CO line, optical depth effects unmodelled, short-spacing problem in ALMA data

evidence.quote: longer observation times, preferably including lines associated with several CO excitations, are needed

referee_caveats_inferred: No radiative transfer despite likely optical thickness
Offset correction and binning choices arbitrary
